name: Infrared Pit Organ Induction
description: Introduces pit viper thermoreceptor organs in shallow depressions on the cheekbones, providing passive infrared sensing. The user perceives heat sources as a spatial overlay — warm bodies glow, engines radiate, recently touched surfaces leave thermal handprints. The sensation is processed as a new spatial sense rather than vision — users describe it as 'feeling' heat at a distance. Effective range is approximately 10 meters for human-body-temperature sources. The pit organs are visible as small, slightly concave patches on the cheeks, each about the size of a thumbprint. Some users have them installed symmetrically; others add additional pits along the jawline for wider coverage. The modification is prized by security professionals, hunters, and anyone who needs to detect concealed people in darkness.
source_organism: Crotalus oreganus (western rattlesnake), Morelia viridis (green tree python)
procedure: Facial subdermal surgery with retroviral thermoreceptor growth, 1 session
reversibility: Surgically removable; leaves small facial scars at pit sites
side_effects: Phantom heat sensations during calibration period
Overwhelming input near industrial heat sources
Facial pit organs are visible and identifiable
Cold environments feel 'loud' — the contrast between cold air and warm bodies becomes intense
social_perception: Professional and somewhat intimidating. Visible pit organs mark the user as someone with predator-adjacent senses. Some people find the cheek depressions unsettling. Military and security culture considers them practical; street culture considers them aggressive.
story_hooks: A thermal-sense user tracks a target through walls by their body heat — only to discover the target is running cold, far too cold for a living person
A Gravemoss Biofoundry batch produces hypersensitive pits that can detect thermal signatures through most building materials, turning recipients into unwitting surveillance assets
